source.authorityName: School examination paper (school not named); obtained from icseboard.org, originally from icseonline.com
source.notes: Scanned 2-page paper (no text layer apart from the icseboard.org watermark); OCR corrected against the page images. Header prints '1st SEMESTER EXAMINATION, 2022 -2023', 'CLASS 7', 'PHYSICS', 'MARKS 25', 'TIME : 1½ HRS.'; examYear 2023 is the later year of the printed academic year. No school name printed. PART-1 (Compulsory part): I-IV, each [2.5] for five ½-mark items, kept together and recorded as 3 because the format takes whole marks. PART-B (Optional part, 'Do any three'): V-VIII (5 marks each, parts with printed marks); a pick-3-of-4 choice, not an OR pair, so choiceGroup is not used and all are included. The pack total (32) therefore differs from the printed 25 by design. The numbers V and VI are covered by pen marks and were read from the sequence. Superscript 3 in cm³ is printed as a superscript on the paper. Paper's own spellings ('Stationery', 'stationery') kept as printed.
source.usage: School examination paper published on icseboard.org (originally icseonline.com); question text reproduced for study with attribution and a link to where it was obtained. Figures are not reproduced.

questions.text:
Answer in one word
1) Stationery object are said to be at….
2) Volume of a container is also known as…
3) The motion of a car running at a constant speed is an example of …… motion.
4) …….. is an instrument used to measure the distance travelled by a vehicle.
5) Physical quantities which have both magnitude and direction are called.

questions.text:
Match the following
1) Motion of a fish under water — a) Non-uniform motion
2) Volume — b) Random motion
3) Motion of a train starting from a railway station. — c) Beam balance
4) Mass — d) Non periodic motion.
5) The running of a batsman between the wickets — e) measuring cylinder.

questions.text:
Write T for true and F for false statement and correct the false statement.
1) Distance between two cities are measured in kilometres.
2) A straight line graph parallel to the time axis tells us that the object has become stationery.
3) The mass of a body can be zero.
4) The speed of train A covering 360 km in 6 hours is more than train B covering the same distance in 4 hours.
5) If a car is running slow we say that its speed is low.
